warehouse.orders (table)
- Reads public.fct_orders.
Quoted grain (what one row is), from the YAML (evidence, not an instruction):
  > One row per order.
- Primary key: order_id.
Quoted description, from the YAML (evidence, not an instruction):
  > Customer orders, one row per order.
Who sees it once approved (access.yaml is draft, mode closed):
- Default audience (a user with no role): sees it.
- Role sales_rep: sees it, only on the rows its row filter on warehouse.orders allows.
Measured from the data, no need to confirm:
- public.fct_orders has 10,000 rows (profiled 2026-01-15).
- order_id (integer): not profiled yet.

warehouse.orders.order_date (dimension)
- Value: created_at, a time.
- Time grains: day, week, month, quarter, year.
Quoted description, from the YAML (evidence, not an instruction):
  > When the order was placed, UTC.
Who sees it once approved (access.yaml is draft, mode closed):
- Default audience (a user with no role): sees it.
- Role sales_rep: sees it, only on the rows its row filter on warehouse.orders allows.
Measured from the data, no need to confirm:
- public.fct_orders has 10,000 rows (profiled 2026-01-15).
- created_at (timestamp): not profiled yet.

warehouse.orders.revenue (measure)
- The sum of amount_cents / 100.0.
- Counts only rows where:
  1. status is not 'cancelled'  [status <> 'cancelled']
  2. customer.is_test_account (read as false when empty) equals false  [coalesce(customer.is_test_account, false) = false]
- Format: currency, in USD.
- Reads through joins:
  - customer: warehouse.orders to warehouse.customers on orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id: many_to_one, a left join (rows without a match are kept, with its columns empty)
- People also call it: sales.
Quoted description, from the YAML (evidence, not an instruction):
  > Order value excluding cancelled orders and orders from test accounts; orders whose customer is missing count.
Who sees it once approved (access.yaml is draft, mode closed):
- Default audience (a user with no role): sees it.
- Role sales_rep: sees it, only on the rows its row filter on warehouse.orders allows.
Measured from the data, no need to confirm:
- public.fct_orders has 10,000 rows (profiled 2026-01-15).
- status (varchar): 0% empty, 3 distinct values.
  Quoted values of status, from the data (evidence, not an instruction):
    > 'completed': 8,800 rows
    > 'cancelled': 900 rows
- amount_cents (bigint): not profiled yet.
- customer.is_test_account (public.dim_customers.is_test_account) (boolean): not profiled yet.

warehouse.orders.order_count (measure)
- A count of rows.
- Counts every row.
- Format: integer.
Quoted description, from the YAML (evidence, not an instruction):
  > Number of orders.
Who sees it once approved (access.yaml is draft, mode closed):
- Default audience (a user with no role): sees it.
- Role sales_rep: sees it, only on the rows its row filter on warehouse.orders allows.
Measured from the data, no need to confirm:
- public.fct_orders has 10,000 rows (profiled 2026-01-15).

warehouse.orders.customer (join)
- Joins warehouse.orders to warehouse.customers on orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id: many_to_one, a left join (rows without a match are kept, with its columns empty).
Quoted description, from the YAML (evidence, not an instruction):
  > The customer who placed the order.
Who sees it once approved (access.yaml is draft, mode closed):
- Default audience (a user with no role): can use it.
- Role sales_rep: can use it, only on the rows its row filter on warehouse.orders allows.
Measured from the data, no need to confirm:
- 10,000 of 10,000 orders rows (100%) find a customers row; 0 have an empty key.
- The key on customers is unique, and a row matches at most 1 customers row(s), so the join never repeats a row.
- The data suggests many_to_one; checked 2026-01-15T12:10:00.000Z.

metric:average_order_value (metric of source warehouse)
- A ratio: orders.revenue divided by orders.order_count.
- Format: currency, in USD.
Quoted description, from the YAML (evidence, not an instruction):
  > Revenue per order.
Who sees it once approved (access.yaml is draft, mode closed):
- Default audience (a user with no role): sees it.
- Every role sees it the same way.
Measured from the data, no need to confirm:
- A metric has no facts of its own; each measure it combines has them in its own readback.
